override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. dolla is a SR/Wind/Supporter Burst II with a pure-support kit: one team-wide ATK buff (S1), a dual-branch escalating S2 (team burst-cooldown reduction on Full Burst entry + a stacking ATK/CritRate/CritDamage team buff on her own burst casts), and a single-target nuke burst. All three buff branches are team-wide (`allies`, self included — the kit says 'all allies' with no exclusion). S2's two headers are distinct blocks with DIFFERENT triggers ('entering Full Burst' vs 'using Burst Skill') and are modeled separately per the trigger-identity rule; collapsing them to one trigger would be a scope error. The burst is a flat single hit with no rider, no DoT, no weapon swap, no stacks, and no ammo/reload/fire-rate modifier — so there are no weapon-state, Hit-Rate, heal/shield, or stack-currency lines to audit. The only genuinely kit-silent quantity is S1's activation, flagged above.

'Each subsequent effect triggers all effects before it' → effects:[{kind:'escalating', steps:[…]}], the Liter-style primitive (Nth activation applies steps 1..N).
escalating step 1 = burstCdr seconds 1.82, target allies. Burst-cooldown reduction is a rotation-mover, never skippable.
escalating step 2 = burstCdr seconds 2.2 (cumulative with step 1 on activation ≥2, per the escalating semantics).
escalating step 3 = burstCdr seconds 2.6. oncePerBattle intentionally NOT set — the kit states no once-per-battle limit.
SECOND block, trigger {kind:'burstCast'} — 'when using Burst Skill' is the owner's own cast (HARD RULE: burst-cast ≠ full-burst-enter; conflating over-credits in multi-B2 comps).
escalating step 1 = buff atkPct 7.72 durationSec 5, target allies. Separate buff key from S1's ATK line (different block/source), so both co-exist.
escalating step 2 = buff critRatePct 4.21 durationSec 5. UNSCOPED crit — the line does not say 'of normal attacks', so critRatePct not critRateNormalPct.

flags.reasoning: The skill1 prose carries NO activation clause at all — only a target header and a stat line. Per the ALWAYS-⚑ taxonomy (item 2: 'a line the text gives NO trigger for') the trigger and its cadence are outside the input domain. Base burst cooldown 20s is the only cadence number available for this unit, used as the interval proxy; the first-fire phase (t=sec vs t=0) is a stated convention, not a measurement. A 5s buff on a 20s interval yields ~25% team-wide uptime — if the real cadence is faster this materially under-credits the whole team's ATK.
flags.recipe: From a fight recording with dolla in the team, log ally ATK-buff refreshes: count the number of distinct 16.16% ATK applications over 180s and their spacing. If spacing ≈ the datamined skillCooldownsSec[0] for dolla, set interval sec to that value; if the buff is continuously present, re-model as {kind:'passive'} with the duration dropped. Cross-check against data/*.json skill-cooldown fields before assuming the 20s burst cd is the skill cd.

flags.reasoning: 'Activates when using Burst Skill' read literally = the OWNER's burst cast, so the ATK/CritRate/CritDamage escalation only advances on rotations where dolla actually casts her Burst II. This is the trigger-identity HARD RULE; the alternative (fullBurstEnter) would advance the escalation on every team Full Burst and over-credit whenever another Burst II unit takes the slot. Confidence in the literal read is HIGH; the flag is on the DIVERGENCE RISK, since dolla is a Burst II and multi-B2 comps are common — in any comp where she is not the casting B2, this whole branch produces zero.
flags.recipe: Run the unit in a comp with a SECOND Burst II unit and compare against a comp where dolla is the sole B2. If the ATK/crit buffs appear in the rotation where she does NOT cast, the trigger is fullBurstEnter, not burstCast. Buff-apply events (stat atkPct value 7.72) keyed to rotations without a dolla burstCast event settle it directly from the event stream.

flags.estimate: 3 tiers, all three held from activation 3 onward; no cap/reset modeled
flags.reasoning: The kit states three tiers and cumulative stacking ('each subsequent effect triggers all effects before it') but says nothing about what activation 4+ does, nor whether the counter resets on any condition. The escalating primitive applies steps 1..N and saturates at the step count, which is the most conservative literal reading. If the game instead resets the count (per-wave, per-reload, per-anything) the late-fight contribution is over-credited.
flags.recipe: Count burst-cast (or FB-enter) activations over a full 180s fight and check whether the tier-3 crit-damage buff is still applying on the 5th+ activation. For the CDR branch, sum the observed burst-cooldown reductions across the fight against the modeled cumulative 1.82+2.2+2.6 = 6.62s per activation from #3 onward — the full-burst count is the sensitive observable.

flags.reasoning: noFb:true is NOT a per-kit measurement here — it follows the project-verified fact that a burst cast lands before the Full Burst window opens, so the +50% major cannot apply. noRange:true is the universal rider convention. crit:true is the schema-default posture for burst damage (rolls at the caster's sheet rate); core is omitted because the text does not say 'core strike damage'. Each is a convention rather than an observation, so flagged rather than shipped silently.
flags.recipe: Read the burst popup in footage: an orange/crit-iconed popup confirms crit eligibility; comparing the popup value against 734.69% × final ATK × (bucket product) with and without the ×1.5 FB major confirms the noFb posture. A red 'CORE HIT' popup on the burst would refute the no-core assumption.

flags.estimate: datamined values as given; not overridden
flags.reasoning: Mandatory ⚑ per the taxonomy (item 1): rate_of_fire and reloadFrames are known-unreliable datamine fields. dolla's kit carries no ammo/reload/fire-rate/charge-speed modifier of its own, so nothing in the override touches the weapon economy — but her normal-attack damage contribution rests entirely on these unvalidated numbers.
